subject: Urgent: Placely streaming chat — sudden connection drops and p99 latency during evening peak
messages:
From: Sally Chen <sally@placely.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.com>, Placely Platform Ops <ops@placely.com>
Date: Sun, 15 Jan 2028 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: weird — evening spikes causing chat disconnects

Hi Rachel —

We just hit a pretty bad outage window during our evening peak (17:45–18:20 PT). ~8% of SSE connections were dropped and our customer-facing webchat showed long stalls; p95 latency went from ~220ms to 1.7s and p99 spiked to ~6.2s. We attached a few graphs from our observability and a connection log sample.

This is the second evening in a row with the same pattern and it’s impacting paywall conversions. Can we get an immediate mitigation and an ETA for a fix? Our CS and ops teams are getting pressure from Product.

Attached: placely_p99_graphs.png, sse_connection_dump-20280115.log

—Sally
Sally Chen
Head of Platform Reliability, Placely
From: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.com>
To: Sally Chen <sally@placely.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 15 Jan 2028 09:28:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: weird — evening spikes causing chat disconnects

Thanks for the data, Sally — I’m sorry you’re seeing this. We’re treating as P0.

Immediate actions:
- I’ve looped in infra and the serving team (Dev/Marcus) to look at hotspotting and connection behavior.
- Can you confirm whether the dropped connections are all using our SSE endpoint (/v1/chat/stream) or a mix with WS? (I see SSE in the logs but want to be sure.)
- We’ll stand up a scrubbed call at 10:00 PT to review traces; if that’s too late, tell me and we’ll move earlier.

We’ll also prepare a customer impact note and a temporary mitigation plan (traffic shaping, aggressive keepalive, fall back to short-polling for affected sessions) — I’ll share options in the next hour.

—Rachel
Rachel Kim
Account Lead (Strategic Accounts), Redwood Inference
From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 15 Jan 2028 09:42:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: weird — evening spikes causing chat disconnects

Quick initial findings from logs and traces:
- The spikes correlate with short-lived GC pauses on a subset of g4 nodes handling TESLA-quantized models (hot shard behavior).
- We also see increased connection churn at the API layer — the front proxy is doing aggressive connection resets when its outbound queue length crosses a threshold.
- SSE client heartbeats are arriving as expected; the proxy is dropping outbound frames while the model kernel stalls. That explains the disconnect+latency combo.

Immediate mitigations I can push now (non-disruptive):
1) Reduce the proxy outbound queue threshold to avoid sudden resets (push now).
2) Enable a temporary per-account concurrency cap for Placely (default -> 0.75x) to reduce burst pressure (requires coordination with Rachel).
3) On longer term: move Placely traffic to a quieter pool (can be done with a 30-minute planned cutover).

I’ll push 1 and instrument; if we still see issues we’ll move to 2 and plan 3.

—Dev
Dev Patel
Staff SRE, Redwood Inference
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 15 Jan 2028 10:05:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: weird — evening spikes causing chat disconnects

Thanks Dev — I agree with the plan. Additional notes from serving:
- The quantized kernels for the model variant Placely uses show increased tail latency when token-generation batches exceed 48 concurrent inflight requests; we’re seeing batching backpressure that cascades to connection stalls.
- Short-term we can: (A) force a lower max_batch_size for Placely’s model variant (reduces throughput but lowers tail), or (B) route Placely to a slightly smaller model variant with a better worst-case kernel path. Both are reversible.

I recommend we do 1) proxy threshold tweak (Dev), 2) immediate per-account concurrency cap at 0.7x, 3) if still noisy, flip routing to smaller model variant for the 3-hour peak window tonight and monitor.

Can Rachel confirm you have customer signoff for a temporary cap or model downgrade? I’ll prepare the route change playbook — it’s about a 12–15 minute planned cutover with 5-minute warmup.

—Marcus
Marcus Lin
Principal Engineer, Serving Runtime
From: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.com>
To: Sally Chen <sally@placely.com>, Jordan Lee <jordan@placely.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 15 Jan 2028 11:02:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: weird — evening spikes causing chat disconnects

Sally — thanks for the quick turn. Customer update:
- We’ll apply a temporary per-account concurrency cap at 70% of your normal burst rate tonight during 17:30–19:30 PT and keep an active watch.
- If the cap does not reduce connection drops, we’ll route your traffic to an alternate model variant for the same window. That swap is reversible and we will run it as a short maintenance with minimal impact.
- We’ll provide a post-mortem and credit offer if the behavior persists.

Please reply here with a quick YES on the temporary cap so we can implement before tonight’s peak.

—Rachel

Laura — please own outreach for customer success follow-up and coordinate any runbook walkthroughs.

Date: Wed, 18 Jan 2028 16:40:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: weird — evening spikes causing chat disconnects — resolution and next steps

Quick closure note:
- We implemented the proxy threshold change and a per-account concurrency cap (0.7x) on Jan 15. Tonight’s 17:30–19:30 PT window showed a 75% reduction in connection resets and p99 reduced from ~6.2s to ~1.1s.
- We performed a controlled routing to a smaller model variant for the peak window on Jan 16 and observed similar improvements with minimal feature regressions.
- Dev/Marcus are scheduling a follow-up to harden kernel-level scheduling and improve batching heuristics; target delivery: Feb 5.
- Priyom has shared the credit proposal; Laura will do a post-mortem call with Placely this week.

Thanks everyone for the fast turnaround — Sally, appreciate your patience. We’ll keep monitoring and I’ll ping once the permanent fix lands.

Attachments included: post-incident graphs and a short timeline.

—Rachel
Rachel Kim
Account Lead (Strategic Accounts), Redwood Inference
